newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan newspapers say rebel areas recaptured.
newsitem.headline: Sudan newspapers say rebel areas recaptured.

text.p: Sudanese newspapers said on Wednesday government troops recaptured areas in central Sudan which had been under rebel control for at least 10 years and released hundreds of people trapped there.

"The People's Defence Forces undertook a successful campaign at the mountains around Dilling (in Southern Kordofan state), and on the border of Rashad and Kadguli provinces," the government newspaper Sudan al-Hadith reported.
The daily named areas "cleared from the rebels" as Abyad town, which lies some 150 km (94 miles) away from Dilling, al-Mur, Jebel Makar, Sharaf and Shambarna.

There was no independent confirmation of the report. The rebel Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA) has been fighting the government for almost 13 years and has formed a coalition with northern rebels to topple the Islamist leadership.

Abdel Jabar Hussein Osman, commissioner of Dilling, told the privately-owned Akhbar al-Youm newspaper the areas recaptured had been under rebel control for at least 10 years. "The area is also of economic importance as it supplies the states of the country with food," he added.

Sudan al-Hadith said government troops had also taken control for the first time in 13 years the road linking Talodi town in the southeast with Malakal, one of the main towns in the south. It also said the route between Talodi and Kadguli in the east was in state hands.
The newspapers also said that the rebels had imprisoned more than 200 people in the areas and that they forced them to carry arms to garrisons in the south.
